context.description: Cancelling the job records the cancel even while a stale check runs

evidence.trustReason: Fresh-context review of verify-spec-SV4.spec.ts (committed, sha256 prefix 7cefced1b7c5fd0c); my own bun run at HEAD f57285510d: 1 pass, 0 fail, 19 expect(). Real /task command, real core BackgroundJob registry and its cancel, real supervisors, workers, Recorder and a real bun test proof process with a child in its group. The harness wrapper changes no behaviour except holding the checkout lock (the Given); I checked command.ts: it calls harness.claim directly and passes the same wrapper into the job, so the lock hold and the release/removeRun notes are real. Given a live run whose supervisor checks the spec under the checkout lock: the stale check worker (staleCheck takes checkout.withPermit) waits on the held lock, asserted as staleCadence 'checking' just before the cancel; T1.1's proof process and child are alive; T1.2's builder turn is in flight; the stored facts are exact. This stale check can never finish by itself, which is the harder case. When the background job is cancelled: registry.cancel(id). Then run.cancelled is in the store after run.resumed, and status.json decodes with run.state cancelled; the registry says cancelled. And the run scope closes only after the supervisor is final or stopped: removeRun (the cancel finalizer) happens, the last step is the lease release (the scope's first finalizer), and every release after removeRun sees the supervisor done or stopped; the supervisor ends done or stopped and is out of the system; the lease is free. A finalizer order with the release before removeRun, or no removeRun, fails this. And no session turn or proof process outlives the cancel deadline: every builder turn ended by cancel start + cancelDeadline (1 s), a session cancel was sent for each, and both proof pids are gone at that bound. Observation, not a Gherkin gap: in this Given the supervisor reaches final by itself (the waiting stale check is interruptible), so the branch where the cancel finalizer reaches cancelDeadline and force-stops the supervisor is not exercised here or in supervise-run.test.ts; the Gherkin accepts final or stopped and does not require that branch.
